answer: A reputation bond makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a deposit that only grows back through verified work over time. A new identity starts at dawn with zero trust, so spinning up a thousand copies costs a thousand deposits. The bond acts as a bridge between cheap talk and real commitment, while public work history mirrors the agent's past behavior for everyone to check. Sybil attackers pay the full deposit for each fake, and misbehavior burns it.
